newsitem.title: UK: Eadie to miss profit expectations for year.
newsitem.headline: Eadie to miss profit expectations for year.

text.p: Eadie Holdings Plc said on Thursday it would not meet profits expectations for the current year due to an orders slowdown and the rescheduling of some orders into next year.

The maker of distribution and healthcare equipment also said its profits had been hurt by restructuring expenses of 500,000 stg , as well as other non-recurring costs and a small loss on the disposal of its loss-making unit, Pentwyn Precisions.

"As a result of these factors, the board of Eadie does not expect the profit before taxation of the second half to exceed the level of profitability reported for the first half of the year," the company said in a statement.
Eadie added it was confident of significantly improved earnings for 1997 and proposed maintaining its final dividend for the current year at 0.8p per share.
Eadie said trading in several operations failed to show the traditional upturn after the summer shutdowns.
At its Ross & Bonnyman unit, for example, significant contracts had not been placed by customers and were unlikely to materialise, the company said.
